label: Алебастровый
purpose: Additional selectable hero portrait; likeness requested by the user, not a new global style reference

steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / portrait variant.
Create ONE NEW standalone 1024 × 1536 PNG portrait of an androgynous adult human playable hero for the dark gothic fantasy game Heroes of Orvesk. This is a new sibling portrait, not a copy of the attached one.
INPUT IMAGE 1: public/portraits/character-03-ivory.png — user-selected reference for the character's appearance and family resemblance ONLY. Keep the recognizable combination of pale subtly weathered skin, light grey eyes, short tousled ash-blond / silver-blond hair with darker roots, refined long nose, elongated face and attentive restrained expression. Visually ambiguous gender: balance soft and defined planes, no beard or stubble, no makeup, exaggerated lashes, massive jaw, heavy masculine brow, or pronounced Adam's apple. A grown adult around 30, not a child and not a glamour model. A subtle individual asymmetry is welcome.
ALLOWED / REQUIRED CHANGES from reference: rebuild composition to the NEW head-position standard below; vary the arrangement and parting of hair instead of tracing the same locks; replace the high wrapped neck scarf with a simple dark charcoal linen tunic with a shallow offset V slit, a low soft folded collar on one side and a visible worn seam. The throat should not be wrapped in the same scarf. Change the fabric folds and neckline construction, not merely its color. Keep clothing quiet and dark. No jewelry, headgear, armor, weapons, ornament, props, frame, text or watermark.
CURRENT ART DIRECTION (governs rendering, do not merely filter the reference):
A dark gothic PAINTED fantasy illustration, sculpturally constructed volume, strong chiaroscuro, tactile dry painted surface. Fine interrupted dry-brush strokes and scumbling FOLLOW the face's form. Face and gaze are most resolved; matte skin has irregular painted half-tones, not photographic pore detail. Hair is grouped into clearly readable locks and light masses; fabric is simplified into large broken angular folds and rough lit edges. Do not draw every pore, hair and thread with equal precision. No photorealism, staged photograph, photo with a grain overlay, glossy or smooth CGI, wax skin, beauty retouching, neon, cartoon, anime, low-poly planes or large impasto strokes obscuring anatomy. Muted graphite, grey-brown, aged linen and restrained living skin undertones. Subtle cool bone-pale emphasis without bleaching all tonal variation. Opaque near-black charcoal backdrop with a very subdued dark tonal patch behind the head; no scenery.
LIGHTING: a SINGLE directional key from ABOVE FRONT IMAGE LEFT. Brightest on face and upper planes, deep readable shadows; shoulders and outer clothing dissolve into the backdrop. No uniform rim light. Keep human skin organic, not a stone sculpture.
COMPOSITION: three-quarter head, nose AND gaze distinctly toward IMAGE RIGHT; both eyes visible. Do not mirror the input. Head and upper shoulders only, not waist. Natural adult anatomy with whole head fully on canvas. Position the whole head rather than distort proportions: head mass horizontal center about X=50% (47–53% of width), width about 70% (64–76%). Deliberate dark headroom: top of main hair/head at Y=12% height (10–14%, target184px). Mean eye line Y=38% (36–40%, target584px). Bottom of chin Y=64% (61–67%, target983px).
This image must work both as a complete rectangle 2:3 and in a round avatar using cover at object-position:50% 25%. At 1024×1536 the avatar samples source x0..1024,y128..1152. Keep important face features inside safe circle center(512,640), radius460.8. Do not draw a circle, marks or guides. Maintain a calm, readable, androgynous face at thumbnail size.

Use case: identity-preserve / composition adjustment.
Image 1 is the original character identity reference. Image 2 is the NEW portrait to adjust. Start from IMAGE 2 and preserve its exact character, androgynous adult face, skin tone, grey eyes, ash-blond hair, RIGHT-facing three-quarter pose, upper-left lighting, painterly dry-brush rendering, low dark tunic neckline and visible seam. Do not restore the scarf from image 1. No mirroring.
ONLY adjust framing to our new standard. Image 2 currently has too little headroom and its head is too large. Uniformly reduce the entire head and neck about 10% and move the composition down so the main hair silhouette begins about y=180 (12% of canvas height), not near the top. Keep the whole head mass centered at x=512. Mean eye line should be y=584 (38% height); bottom chin about y=980 (64% height), main head width about720px (70% width). Preserve natural anatomy by scaling and moving the whole head, do not stretch the face. Repaint / extend plain near-black charcoal backdrop into the new headroom, connect neck and upper shoulders naturally into the lower dark garment. Still a close head-and-upper-shoulders portrait; no more torso than necessary.
Canvas remains 1024x1536, opaque PNG. No borders, circle, guides, text, weapons, jewelry or new accessories. Important facial features must fit round source crop center(512,640), radius460.8. Preserve the new tunic and texture of image 2.

Use case: identity-preserve, tiny framing correction only.
Image 1 is the original identity reference. Image 2 is the current finished new portrait, with the correct new tunic and painterly style. Use image 2 as the edit target.
The last framing change moved the head a little too low. Raise the ENTIRE painted person (head, hair, face, neck and garment together) by ONLY 45 pixels on the unchanged 1024x1536 canvas (about 3% of canvas height). Do not reduce or enlarge anything. Do not reframe or rescale the face. This is a very small upward translation only, preserving all face shapes and proportions, RIGHT gaze, exact expression, androgyny, hair, clothing, dry painted texture and lighting. Extend the dark tunic at the bottom as necessary; retain the opaque charcoal background.
The visible main hair silhouette should end up about y=195–205, eyes about y=590–610, chin about y=940–980; face remains horizontally centered. No further changes to identity, materials, rendering, clothing, color, pose or head size; no circle, guides, text, frame, added accessories or mirroring.
